thesis: Friday's AIDEA meeting isn't where Alaska's data center question gets decided. Nothing data center is on the board's agenda, the live data center clock is DNR's Houston reconsideration window that opens November 30th and could close after the handoff, and the version of this that helps Alaska win is rules before tenants.
falsifiability: False if the November 27th or December 4th agenda adds a data center or Alaska Data Corp item (c13, c14, c36), or if DNR rules on the Houston reconsideration requests before December 7th (c32, c1), which would put the land question back on the outgoing clock.
supporting_facts: The pause request targets board action (c2) and the pending agenda lists ANWR, Ambler and Port MacKenzie with no data center item (c36); the board met behind closed doors and took no action (c12) and resumes November 27th (c13).

The data center pieces already moved through other doors: the $20M board vote to the AIDEA-owned Alaska Data Corp (c9, c10) and DNR's November 10th transfer of about 6,800 acres near Houston at no cost (c20), land AIDEA said in July could host scalable data centers among other uses (c22).

The land has its own clock: reconsideration due November 30th, then 30 days for DNR (c32), so an answer could land under a governor who supports a moratorium until rules exist (c11) and has said he'd completely reassess AIDEA's work (c34).
counterpoint_to_honor: Two fair cases, each given a scene. AIDEA's: Ruaro says this is due diligence, not a rush (c15), with record revenue three years running (c16); Dunleavy says Alaskans elected him for a full term (c17); and the transfer was cut from nearly 20,000 acres (c21) with salmon streams and trails protected (c27) and a reversion clause (c26). The community's: more than 2,300 comments mostly opposed (c28), a unanimous Assembly (c29), the borough pointing to Point MacKenzie and its $180M rail bed (c30, c31), and a pending lawsuit (c33). And DNR says it approved a transfer, not a use (c35), while AIDEA's director called a data center there implausible in October (c38).
valence: curious and constructive. The capital pitch behind AI infrastructure is real (c37, the pitch not a project) and Alaska has a funded vehicle (c10). Rules first loses nothing that exists today, because AIDEA itself listed no tenant, power source, cooling or schedule (c24). Neither side is a villain; the film ends on a question of order.
who_it_serves: Mat-Su residents and the borough, who have a live way to be heard by November 30th (c30, c32); legislators and the incoming team watching the handoff; and anyone who wants Alaska to land AI infrastructure capital (c37) on a site that won't be fought in court (c33).
second_movement: DNR says its decision covers the transfer, not the use (c35), and the borough isn't refusing industry, it names other sites (c30, c31). So even the land clock doesn't decide what gets built. What decides it is whether rules arrive before a tenant does (c11, c24).

runner_up_angles.angle: The lame-duck rush is a power grab
runner_up_angles.lost_because: claims a motive the record doesn't show: closed session, no action (c12), a request not an order (c2), Ruaro rejects rushing (c15)

runner_up_angles.angle: A pause throws away Alaska's head start in the AI data center race
runner_up_angles.lost_because: no data center vote is pending (c36), no tenant, power or schedule (c24), no project identified (c25); the head start is a pitch (c37)

runner_up_angles.angle: Nothing data center is moving, so the fight is theatre
runner_up_angles.lost_because: the $20M vote is done (c10), the land moved November 10th (c20), the reconsideration clock runs past the handoff (c32), 2,300+ comments (c28)

cross_challenge: Three analysts (structural, enthusiast, dramatist) each red-teamed two of the three rivals above; all three converged on the separate-clock reading. The enthusiast's 'rules first loses nothing that exists today' is grafted as the button; the dramatist's community-as-civic-process is the Act 3 scene; the structural reading's 'transfer, not use' is the second movement.
absence_checks: No data center item: read the November 24th continued agenda in full (executive session topics, Resolutions G26-05, G26-07, G26-01, directors comment). The governor-elect's statement doesn't mention data centers (Must Read Alaska quotes it at length). Neither ADN November 11th nor the pause coverage mentions AI; the only AI line is the Plural CEO in the InvestNorth launch release.
distinct_from_recent: 10-20 asked whether the land should pass before anyone can say what will be built (preliminary decision); 11-13 asked rules first or money first for tokenized stakes; this film is about which clock decides, after the transfer and the pause request.
